data.name: CliHelp
data.value:
2Password {0} --inspect <package> [--report <new.json>] --inspect-self [--report <new.json>] --extract <package> --output <new-directory> --password-stdin [--verify-first] [--report <new.json>] --extract-self --output <new-directory> --password-stdin [--verify-first] [--report <new.json>] --create <source> --output <new.exe> --passwords-stdin [--compression zstd|brotli|none] [--layout auto|embedded|detached] [--recovery-percent 0|5|10|20] [--stub <published-exe>] [--report <new.json>] --verify-recovery <par2> [--report <new.json>] --repair-recovery <par2> [--report <new.json>] --export-recovery-source <new.tar.xz> [--report <new.json>] --language en|zh-CN Optional for every operation, including --help.
Passwords are accepted only through redirected standard input, encoded as strict UTF-8 without BOM detection. Creation expects a JSON string array. Extraction reads the exact password and removes only one final newline. Defaults: Zstd compression, automatic layout, 10% PAR2 recovery data. Detached packages require both the EXE and .2pw in the same folder. Keep all generated .par2 files too. Normal extraction authenticates data in one streaming pass. On detected corruption, matching PAR2 data can repair it before retrying authenticated extraction. --verify-first adds a complete PAR2 verification pass before extraction. Existing output files and directories are never overwritten or merged. Recovery exit status: 0 = healthy/success, 1 = repairable, 2 = insufficient recovery data.
